hypothesis: Quantum models (QNN/VQC/QSVM/CLT-QNN/CLT-VQC) make complementary errors to classical models (SVM-RBF/RF/LogReg/XGBoost) on the locked controlled validation set
architecture: all classical x quantum pairs (20 pairs, 4 classical x 5 quantum)
result: All 20 pairwise error correlations are positive (range 0.26-0.89); none negative. Q-statistics mostly near 1.0 (near-total agreement on correct/incorrect cases). QSVM correlates almost perfectly with every classical model (corr 0.84-0.89) since it uses the same 4 selected features and a similar kernel decision boundary.
reason_rejected: No pair shows the negative or near-zero error correlation that would justify a complementarity-driven fusion advantage; quantum models mostly fail on the same validation frauds classical models already catch, or fail additionally (e.g. VQC: quantum-only-frauds captured is <=2 for every classical partner while classical-only-frauds-caught is 12-21)
what_was_learned: On this small (n=100) locked validation subset, quantum arms trained on the same 4 mutual-information-selected features do not provide an error-diversity advantage over classical baselines; VQC and QNN standalone PR-AUC (not reported here, see experiment_log.csv) trail the classical baselines. Per protocol, fusion (step 2) is still tested empirically since point estimates on n=100 are noisy, but the a priori complementarity hypothesis is rejected on this evidence.

hypothesis: SVM-RBF+CLT-QNN score fusion beats SVM-RBF alone
result: point estimate PR-AUC delta +0.0427 on val (n=100), but 2000-resample paired bootstrap 95% CI = [-0.0130, +0.1140], crosses zero
reason_rejected: not statistically distinguishable from noise at this sample size
what_was_learned: apparent fusion gains at n=100 validation are not reliable; would need a much larger controlled subset or multi-seed confirmation before any claim

hypothesis: Adding a CLT-QNN score as a stacking feature beats classical-only stacking
result: point estimate PR-AUC delta +0.0066 on val (n=100), but 2000-resample paired bootstrap 95% CI = [-0.0061, +0.0234], crosses zero
what_was_learned: marginal quantum-feature contribution in stacking is indistinguishable from zero at this sample size
